question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated authority and the absence of viable internal challenges underpin trader expectations that he will remain in power through 2026. Extensive purges of senior military and party figures since 2025, including multiple Central Military Commission members, have reinforced his dominance over the People’s Liberation Army and elite networks while eliminating potential rivals. Preparations for the 21st Party Congress in late 2027 center on securing a fourth term, with loyalists such as Cai Qi elevated to key vetting and disciplinary roles and no designated successor emerging. Xi, now 73, faces no formal term limits following prior institutional changes, and recent elite gatherings have emphasized continuity rather than transition. Unlikely but plausible shifts could still arise from acute health developments or an unforeseen coalescence of factional resistance ahead of the congress.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains a wide-open contest more than two years before primaries begin, with trader prices reflecting a fragmented field where no candidate has declared and support is dispersed across governors, senators, and House members. Recent DNC approval of a calendar front-loading South Carolina and other diverse states has shaped early positioning, while 2026 midterm results loom as a key test of party momentum ahead of potential announcements. Polling aggregates often show Kamala Harris ahead nationally, yet markets assign higher implied probabilities to Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jon Ossoff, and Gavin Newsom, highlighting trader emphasis on factors like fundraising capacity, regional strength, and perceived general-election viability over raw name recognition. Upcoming midterms, candidate entry decisions, and shifts in early-state surveys could quickly consolidate or redistribute these odds.
